t.5.10.1: In the midst of that palace, the monkey, eager to see Sītā, went to the bowers of creepers, the picture-halls and the night-chambers, yet he did not see her of lovely appearance.
t.5.10.2: Then the great monkey, not seeing that beloved of Raghunandana, reflected: “Surely Sītā is dead, since Maithilī does not come into my sight though I keep searching.”
t.5.10.3: That young woman, devoted to guarding her own virtue and standing firm on the highest noble path, must surely have been slain by this foremost of rākṣasas, whose deeds are utterly wicked.
t.5.10.4: Seeing the women of the king of the rākṣasas, misshapen in form, deformed, lustreless, wide-mouthed, tall and hideous to behold, she, the daughter of the lord Janaka, was undone by fear.
t.5.10.5: Without having seen Sītā, without having shown any manly prowess, and having spent a long time wandering about with the monkeys, there is no way for me to return to Sugrīva, for that monkey is mighty and very harsh in his punishment.
t.5.10.6: The whole inner palace has been searched, and Rāvaṇa's women have been seen, yet the virtuous Sītā is not to be seen. My toil has been in vain.
t.5.10.8: Without having seen her, the daughter of Janaka, what shall I say? Surely, now that the appointed time has passed, they will resort to fasting unto death.
t.5.10.7: What indeed will all the monkeys, gathered together, say to me when I have gone back? 'Having gone there, O hero, what was accomplished by you? Tell us that.'
t.5.10.9: Or what will the aged Jāmbavān say, and that Aṅgada, and the assembled monkeys, to me who have gone to the far shore of the ocean?
t.5.10.10: Freedom from despondency is the root of prosperity; freedom from despondency is the highest happiness. Therefore I shall search once more, in those places where no search has yet been made.
t.5.10.11: For freedom from despondency always drives one forward in all undertakings; it makes fruitful whatever deed a creature performs.
t.5.10.12: Therefore I shall make a supreme effort, born of unflagging resolve, and I shall search the regions guarded by Rāvaṇa that I have not yet seen.
t.5.10.13: The drinking halls were searched, and likewise the flower-houses; the picture galleries too were searched, and again the pleasure-houses.
t.5.10.14: "The lanes among the pleasure-gardens and the palaces on every side remain"; reflecting thus, he began to search once again.
t.5.10.16: Opening the doors and pushing against the door-panels, entering and coming out again, dropping down and leaping up, that great monkey roamed through every open space.
t.5.10.15: The underground chambers, the shrine-halls, and the houses within houses too he explored, leaping up and dropping down, now standing still, now moving on again here and there.
t.5.10.17: In that inner palace of Rāvaṇa there was not a single space, even one of only four fingers' breadth, to which that monkey did not go.
t.5.10.19: There Hanumān saw rākṣasīs of many different forms, misshapen and deformed as well, but he did not see her, the daughter of Janaka.
t.5.10.18: The lanes between the ramparts, the platforms adjoining the shrines, the hollows and the lotus ponds: all of it was searched by him.
t.5.10.21: There Hanūmān saw Nāga maidens with lovely hips and faces like the full moon, but not Sītā of the slender waist.
t.5.10.22: There Hanumān saw the Nāga maidens whom the lord of the Rākṣasas had carried off by force after crushing their people, but he did not see her, the daughter of Janaka.
t.5.10.20: There Hanumān saw excellent Vidyādhara women, unequalled in beauty in the world, but not the delight of Rāghava.
t.5.10.23: Not seeing her, while seeing other excellent women, the mighty-armed one, the mighty-armed Hanūmān, son of Māruta, fell into despair.
t.5.10.24: Seeing the effort of the lords of the monkeys and his leap across the ocean to be in vain, the son of the Wind fell once more into anxious thought.
t.5.10.25: Having descended from the aerial palace, Hanūmān, the son of Māruta, then fell into anxious thought, his mind struck down by grief.
